newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Landslides bury part of Bulgaria's tourist coast.
newsitem.headline: Landslides bury part of Bulgaria's tourist coast.

text.p: Landslides have destroyed roads and some 100 holiday bungalows and villas on Bulgaria's Black Sea coast ahead of this year's tourist season, officials said on Monday.
They said there were two landslides last week above and below two main roads along the coast, linking the port of Varna with the Golden Sands resort and the Albena resort.
Vanyo Dimitrov, head of Civil Defence in Varna Region, said there had been no damage to the Golden Sands resort, visited by thousands of foreign tourists each year.
"The Golden Sands resort is safe and not threatened by the landslides. Tourist holidays in the Golden Sands resort are guaranteed," Dimitrov said.
Local media said more than 20 hectares (50 acres) of a holiday villa zone near Varna had dropped towards the sea. The holiday homes were mostly unoccupied and there were no casualties.

Geologists have been warning of landslides in the area for 50 years and only small buildings were supposed to be permitted there, Bulgarian newspapers said. But big, multi-storey houses had been built recently in breach of regulations.
"Illegal buildings and a lack of drainage are the main causes of the landslides," local media quoted interim construction minister Nikola Karadimov as saying.
Spring floods have covered hundreds of hectares of arable land in eastern Bulgaria and 18 villages are without power, said Lili Kostadinova, spokeswoman for the national civil defence office.
Reservoirs are being closely monitored as some are nearing critical levels and could overflow.
